structure.heading: ITEM 1A Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase: Provided below is a cautionary discussion of what we believe to be the most important risk factors applicable to the Company.
structure.summary:
- Cautionary forward-looking statements outlining that results may differ due to various risks, with references to MD&A and SEC filings (Forms 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K).
- Item 1A Risk Factors:
  - Global macroeconomic, geopolitical, and capital market conditions affecting demand, supply chains, trade policy, inflation, interest/tax rates, and access to capital; 60% of revenue is international.
  - Credit rating sensitivity (AA- S&P, A1 Moody’s, both stable) and potential impacts on borrowing costs and liquidity.
  - Competitive pressures, pricing dynamics, customer ordering patterns, changing preferences, and disruptive technologies (AI, blockchain, analytics).
  - Foreign exchange risk from a strong U.S. dollar on international sales and earnings.
  - Dependence on successful, timely new product development, IP protection, and market acceptance.
  - Volatility and availability of components, raw materials, and energy (including oil and gas), and potential supplier disruptions.
  - Effects of acquisitions, alliances, divestitures, and organizational restructuring; integration and synergy realization risks.
  - Execution risk in productivity initiatives and global business transformation, including multi-year ERP implementation.
  - Cybersecurity and IT infrastructure risks (including third-party providers and ERP standardization), data privacy exposure, and residual insurance limitations.
  - Pension and postretirement plan exposure to market performance, discount rates, asset values, and regulatory changes.
  - Legal and regulatory exposure (product liability, antitrust, IP, environmental, anti-corruption), with outcomes potentially impacting results; details cross-referenced to Note 16.
- Item 1B Unresolved Staff Comments: None.
- Item 2 Properties: Headquarters and major labs in St. Paul, MN; 75 U.S. manufacturing facilities in 29 states; 107 international facilities in 36 countries; majority of properties owned and shared across segments.
- Item 3 Legal Proceedings: Incorporated by reference to Note 16.
- Item 4 Mine Safety Disclosures: Required data for 2018 provided in Exhibit 95 under Dodd-Frank Section 1503.

structure.title: Results of Operations
structure.heading: Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase: Refer to the preceding “Overview” section and the “Performance by Business Segment” section later in MD&A for additional discussion of sales change.
structure.summary:
- Highlights a 2019 closed acquisition: 3M bought the technology business of M*Modal for approximately $0.7 billion in cash and assumed about $0.3 billion of debt; the asset will be reported in the Health Care segment.
- Results of operations overview with emphasis on operating expenses: provides a three-year view (2016–2018) of cost of sales, SG&A, R&D, gain on sales of businesses, and operating margin as percentages of net sales; 2018 operating margin declined primarily due to the Minnesota Natural Resource Damages (NRD) resolution.
- Cost of sales analysis: 2018 increase as a percent of sales driven by foreign currency (net of hedge losses), restructuring tied to the Communication Markets Division, higher raw materials, and higher pension/postretirement and defined contribution expense; partially offset by prior-year charges that did not repeat and selling price increases; 2017 increase driven by strategic investments, portfolio/footprint actions, and FX, partially offset by sourcing savings.
- SG&A: up 14.7% in 2018, largely from Communication Markets Division-related restructuring and the Minnesota NRD resolution; partially offset by non-repeating 2017 optimization charges. Notes ongoing “business transformation” (global ERP and process/service changes) affecting cost of sales, SG&A, and R&D.
- R&D: decreased $49 million in 2018 mainly due to the divestiture of the Communication Markets Division; continued funding of disruptive innovation; R&D was 5.6% of sales in 2018 versus 5.9% in 2017 and 2016.
- Gains on sale of businesses: multiple small divestitures in 2018; major divestiture was the sale of substantially all of the Communication Markets Division to Corning, yielding a $494 million gain (plus $15 million from the remaining German integration services in December); prior-year gains of $586 million (2017) and $111 million (2016).
- Operating income margin reconciliation: breaks down 2018 and 2017 changes by factors—identity management divestiture gain (2017), organic volume/productivity, acquisitions/divestitures, selling price vs. raw materials, FX, legal-related charges, and the Communication Markets Division divestiture plus related restructuring. 2018 full-year margin down 2.3 pts, but up 0.4 pts excluding the Minnesota NRD resolution; Q4 2018 margin flat year-on-year.
- Other expense (income), net: higher interest expense in 2018 and 2017 due to greater debt and rates; a $96 million early debt extinguishment charge in 2017; higher interest income year-on-year; adoption of ASU 2017-07 moves pension/postretirement non-service costs to other expense, with increases in 2018 and 2017.
- Income taxes: effective tax rates—23.4% (2018), 35.5% (2017), 28.3% (2016); significant impacts from U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA), including a $762 million charge in 2017 and $176 million measurement-period adjustments in 2018; outlines TCJA provisions (rate cut, GILTI, FDII, etc.); estimated 2019 ETR of 20–22%.
- Net income attributable to noncontrolling interest: $14 million in 2018, primarily from 3M India Limited (75% owned).
- Currency effects: FX and hedging reduced pre-tax income by $42 million (2018) and $111 million (2017); derivative and other transaction effects reduced pre-tax income by ~$92 million (2018) and ~$152 million (2017).
- Business segment performance and reporting changes effective 2018: expanded dual-credit sales attribution internationally by consolidating customer accounts; centralized certain shared film manufacturing/supply technology into Corporate & Unallocated; adoption of ASU 2017-07 affects segment operating income presentation; maintains five reportable segments.
- Corporate & Unallocated: explains contents (e.g., certain gains/losses, litigation/environmental, restructuring, under/over-absorbed costs, and post-divestiture contract manufacturing/transition services); notes a $1.1 billion increase in 2018 expenses, including $105 million and $22 million restructuring charges related to the Communication Markets Division divestiture and recognition of the $897 million Minnesota NRD resolution.

structure.title: Performance by Business Segment

structure.summary:

- Segment performance highlights:
  - Industrial (37.4% of sales):

Strength in advanced materials, separation/purification, industrial adhesives/tapes, automotive & aerospace, abrasives; auto aftermarket flat. 2018 divestitures included polymer additives compounding and abrasives glass products; earlier divestitures in 2016 (Polyfoam, temporary protective films). Operating income $2.737B; margin 22.3% (+1.3 pts) aided by absence of 2017 portfolio/footprint costs.

Growth in personal safety, commercial solutions, transportation safety; decline in roofing granules. Operating income $1.720B; margin 25.2% (-7.9 pts) primarily due to prior-year divestiture gains and Scott Safety impact; additional 2018 divestiture of certain personal safety monitoring products.
    - 2017: Sales $6.235B (+4.8% total; +6.3% organic). Major portfolio moves: divested safety prescription eyewear; identity management; tolling/ALPR; electronic monitoring; acquired Scott Safety. Margin up 9.5 pts largely from divestiture gains, partly offset by acquisition/investments.
  - Health Care (18.4% of sales):
    - 2018: Sales $6.021B (+2.9% total; +2.6% organic; FX +0.3%). Growth in food safety, health information systems, medical solutions; oral care up internationally; drug delivery declined. Operating income $1.799B; margin 29.9% (-0.2 pts) due to growth investments. Notes: 2017 acquisition of Elution Technologies; February 2019 acquisition of M*Modal’s technology business (AI-powered clinical documentation).

  - Electronics and Energy (16.7% of sales):

Electronics-related up 3% organically (materials solutions up; display flat); energy-related up 5% organically but total energy sales down 10% due to divestitures; Asia Pacific up 4% organically. Divested Communication Markets Division (June) with ~$494M pre-tax gain; sold remaining German systems integration services (Dec) with $15M gain; 2017 divestiture of electrical marking/labeling. Operating income $2.055B; margin 37.6% (+12.6 pts) primarily from divestiture gain.
    - 2017: Sales $5.501B (+11.7% total; +11.6% organic). Strong electronics demand; portfolio/footprint actions and divestiture impacts tempered margin, which rose 1.8 pts net.
  - Consumer (14.6% of sales):
    - 2018: Sales $4.796B (+1.4% total; +1.5% organic; FX -0.1%). Growth in home improvement; stationery/office and home care flat; consumer health care declined. Operating income $1.027B; margin 21.4% (+0.2 pts) aided by non-recurrence of 2017 portfolio/footprint costs.
    - 2017: Sales $4.731B (+3.3% total; +2.7% organic). Growth in consumer health care, home improvement, home care; stationery/office down due to U.S. channel inventory adjustments; margin down 1.8 pts from investments.
- Geographic performance notes: Geography used as a secondary metric; export sales recorded where final customer sales occur; shifts in customer operations can move geographic results; net sales by area not a direct proxy for end-user consumption. Additional geographic data in Note 19; summary in the report’s Overview.

structure.title: New Accounting Pronouncements
structure.heading: New Accounting Pronouncements

structure.summary:
- Goodwill and impairment testing: Valuations used multiple scenarios with different sales growth and terminal value assumptions weighted by management’s estimated probabilities. 3M’s integrated business model and internally developed operations mean many units lack associated goodwill and are not easily sold standalone. The 2018 annual test indicated no goodwill impairment. Potential future impairments could arise from macroeconomic shifts, competitive and customer changes, FX fluctuations, or weighted average cost of capital changes. Long‑lived assets are reviewed upon triggering events, and only portions would be expected to be impaired if charges occur. Ongoing monitoring to continue in 2019.
- Income taxes: Significant judgment applied across jurisdictions under ASC 740 for uncertain tax positions, with reserves adjusted as facts change; ultimate resolutions may differ materially from estimates. 3M recorded net tax expense from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) related to the transition tax on previously unremitted foreign earnings and deferred tax remeasurement; finalized in Q4 2018 (see Note 10).
- New accounting standards: Discussion of new accounting pronouncements is provided in Note 1 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.
- Capital allocation and liquidity strategy: Priority on investing for organic growth (R&D, capex, commercialization), supplemented by complementary acquisitions, plus continued dividends and share repurchases. Strong free cash flow and market access support capital deployment.
- Cash access and repatriation: U.S. operational needs funded by domestic cash flow and capital markets; TCJA provides ongoing opportunities to access international cash. Some foreign earnings remain indefinitely reinvested with no current repatriation plans (see Note 10).
- Short‑term funding: Primary needs met via cash and U.S. commercial paper. Program capacity up to $5 billion with maximum 397‑day maturity; $435 million outstanding at December 31, 2018 (vs. $745 million at December 31, 2017).
- Debt profile and ratings: Strong market access with staggered maturities. Credit ratings: S&P AA‑ (stable) and Moody’s A1 (stable).
- 2018 debt activity: Total debt up approximately $0.7 billion year‑over‑year, driven by $2.25 billion issued in September 2018 and net subsidiary borrowings/FX, partially offset by maturities of $450 million (August 2018) and €500 million (November 2018) medium‑term notes and lower commercial paper at year‑end.
- Shelf and notes programs: WKSI shelf updated February 24, 2017. Medium‑term notes (Series F) program capacity increased to $18 billion; about $15.3 billion issued cumulatively through December 31, 2018 (including Euro‑denominated debt at issuance FX rates).
- Revolving credit facility and covenants: $3.75 billion five‑year revolver maturing March 2021 (accordion up to $5.0 billion), undrawn at year‑end 2018. Covenant requires EBITDA/interest ≥3.0x; actual ≈25x. Covenants do not restrict dividends.
- Other credit support: $243 million of stand‑alone letters of credit and bank guarantees outstanding at December 31, 2018.

structure.title: Financial Condition and Liquidity
structure.heading: Financial Condition and Liquidity
structure.start_phrase: The strength and stability of 3M’s business model and strong free cash flow capability, together with proven capital markets access, positions the Company to be able to add further leverage to its capital structure.
structure.summary:
- Focus of section: 3M’s financial condition, liquidity, capital structure, cash flows, non-GAAP metrics, contractual obligations, and risk management via financial instruments for year-end 2018 with comparisons to 2017/2016.

- Capital allocation and liquidity:
  - Priority on investing for organic growth (R&D, capex, commercialization), supplemented by acquisitions; ongoing cash returns via dividends and share repurchases.
  - Access to U.S. cash flows and capital markets historically sufficient; TCJA enhances ongoing repatriation flexibility while some international earnings remain indefinitely reinvested.
  - Short-term liquidity supported by cash and a U.S. commercial paper program (max $5B; $435M outstanding at 12/31/18).

- Debt and credit profile:
  - Strong market access; staggered maturities; credit ratings AA- (S&P) and A1 (Moody’s), both stable outlooks.
  - Total debt $14.6B at 12/31/18, up $0.7B YoY, reflecting $2.25B notes issued in Sept 2018, partially offset by maturities ($450M USD and €500M) and lower commercial paper.
  - WKSI shelf in place; Series F medium-term notes capacity $18B with ~$15.3B issued to date.
  - Revolving credit facility: $3.75B through March 2021 (undrawn), with a 3.0x minimum EBITDA/interest covenant; actual ~25x at 12/31/18; $243M stand-alone letters of credit/guarantees outstanding.

- Cash and marketable securities:
  - $3.3B total at 12/31/18 ($3.1B foreign, $160M U.S.) vs. 2017’s ~$4.2B total; invested in high-quality bank/fixed income instruments.

- Net debt (non-GAAP):
  - Total debt $14,622M less cash/marketable securities $3,270M = net debt $11,352M (up $1,559M YoY).

- Working capital and balance sheet:
  - Working capital (non-GAAP) $6,465M at 12/31/18, down $125M YoY.
  - Drivers: lower cash/marketable securities; current liabilities decreased (notably short-term debt), which partially offset.
  - AR up $109M on higher sales (FX -$166M; net M&A -$29M). Inventory up $332M, partly due to U.S. ERP deployment (FX -$154M; net M&A -$23M).

- Return on Invested Capital (non-GAAP):
  - ROIC: 22.2% (2018), 21.3% (2017), 22.6% (2016).
  - 2018 impacted by TCJA measurement adjustment, Minnesota NRD resolution, and gain on sale of Communication Markets Division net of related restructuring (combined -2 pts).
  - 2017 decreased due to TCJA and higher commercial paper tied to pension funding (combined -3 pts).
  - 2018 adjusted net income $5,631M; average invested capital $25,318M.

- Cash flows:
  - Operating: $6,439M (2018), up $199M YoY; benefits from higher net income and lower pension contributions; offsets include MN NRD payment, higher taxes, and working capital build (+$406M in 2018 vs +$608M in 2017).
  - Investing: +$222M (2018) vs -$3,086M (2017); capex $(1,577)M; proceeds from divestitures (Communication Markets Division and certain safety products); 2019 capex expected $1.7–$1.9B.
  - Financing: $(6,701)M (2018); net debt increase $933M; share repurchases $(4,870)M; dividends $(3,193)M.

- Detailed debt activity:
  - 2018 issuances: $400M 2021 3.00%; $300M 2024 3.25%; $300M 2024 FRN (3M LIBOR); $600M 2028 3.625%; $650M 2048 4.00%. CP outstanding $435M at year-end.
  - 2017 issuances: $650M 2023 2.25%; $850M 2027 2.875%; $500M 2047 3.625%; $305M debt tender with $96M extinguishment cost.
  - 2016 issuances: €500M 2022 0.375%; €500M 2031 1.50%; $600M 2021 1.625%; $650M 2026 2.25%; $500M 2046 3.125%; repaid $1B due 2016.

- Shareholder returns:
  - Share repurchases: New $10B authorization (Nov 2018); $4.9B repurchased in 2018 (vs $2.1B in 2017; $3.8B in 2016). Expected 2019 buybacks: $2–$4B.
  - Dividends: $3.193B ($5.44/share) in 2018; increased to $1.44/share quarterly in Feb 2019 ($5.76 annual), marking 61 consecutive years of increases.

- Free cash flow (non-GAAP):
  - FCF = Operating cash flow – Capex: $4,862M (2018), $4,867M (2017), $5,242M (2016).
  - FCF conversion: 91% (2018), 100% (2017), 104% (2016).
  - 2018 conversion reduced ~2 pts by TCJA measurement adjustment, MN NRD, and divestiture gain/restructuring; 2017 benefited ~3 pts from TCJA and an additional $600M U.S. pension contribution.

- Off-balance sheet and commitments:
  - No SPEs used. Standard warranties/guarantees and customary indemnifications not expected to be material.
  - Contractual obligations total $22.2B at 12/31/18: debt $14.6B; interest $4.3B; operating leases $1.1B; capital leases $104M; TCJA transition tax $649M (payable over 8 years); unconditional purchase obligations/other $1.4B.
  - Uncertain tax positions long-term portion ($655M) excluded due to timing uncertainty; pension contributions largely discretionary.

- Financial instruments and risk management:
  - Use of FX forwards/options/swaps to hedge currency exposures; mix of fixed/floating-rate debt and interest rate swaps to manage rate risk; commodity risk managed via supply contracts, price protection, and commodity swaps.

structure.title: Financial Instruments

structure.start_phrase: The Company enters into foreign exchange forward contracts, options and swaps to hedge against the effect of exchange rate fluctuations on cash flows denominated in foreign currencies and certain intercompany financing transactions.
structure.summary:

  - Total debt: $14.6 billion (2019: $1.21b; 2020: $1.33b; 2021: $1.70b; 2022: $1.17b; 2023: $1.33b; after 2023: $7.89b)

  - Other includes current portions of uncertain tax positions under ASC 740; long-term uncertain tax liability of $655m excluded due to timing uncertainty

- Financial instruments and market risk management (Item 7A overview):
  - Governance: Senior management oversees risk policies, derivative use, controls, valuation, counterparty approval, and monitoring
  - Counterparty risk: Managed via credit approvals/limits; exposure limited to instrument fair value; counterparties are major international banks
- Foreign exchange risk:
  - Exposure from translation, transactions, and net investments; use of FX forwards/options as cash flow hedges (max horizon 36 months) and for intercompany activities (non-designated)
  - Net investment hedging via FX forwards and foreign currency debt
  - Notional amounts at 12/31/18: $3.4b designated FX hedges; $2.5b non-designated FX; €4.1b of foreign-currency debt designated as net investment hedges
- Interest rate risk:
  - Managed via mix of fixed/floating debt and interest rate swaps designated as fair value hedges
  - Notional of interest rate swaps at 12/31/18: $2.4b (inception-date FX rates)
- Commodity price risk:
  - Managed through supply contracts, price protection agreements, and commodity swaps
  - Hedge accounting: Effective portions recognized in other comprehensive income and reclassified to cost of sales when the hedged transaction impacts earnings

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.heading: ITEM 7A Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.start_phrase: In the context of Item 7A, 3M is exposed to market risk due to the risk of loss arising from adverse changes in foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates and commodity prices.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Excerpt from 3M’s Form 10-K covering Item 7A (Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk) and the opening of Item 8 (Financial Statements and Management’s Responsibility for Financial Reporting).

- Risk governance: Senior management oversees market risk and derivative activities, sets risk policies, approves counterparties, and maintains controls, valuation, monitoring, and reporting procedures.

- Counterparty credit risk: Exposure limited to the fair value of interest rate, currency, commodity swaps, forwards, and options; counterparties are major international banks; no anticipated nonperformance.

- Foreign exchange risk:
  - Exposures: Translation of foreign earnings and cash flows from foreign-denominated transactions; net investments in foreign subsidiaries.
  - Hedging: FX forwards and options designated as cash flow hedges (maximum horizon 36 months); nondesignated forwards to offset intercompany licensing/financing; net investment hedges via FX forwards and foreign currency debt.
  - Notionals at 12/31/2018: $3.4B designated (cash flow or net investment hedges); $2.5B nondesignated; €4.1B foreign-currency debt designated as net investment hedges.

- Interest rate risk:
  - Approach: Mix of fixed and floating debt; use of interest rate swaps designated as fair value hedges.
  - Notionals at 12/31/2018: $2.4B in interest rate swaps. Additional details referenced in Notes 12 and 14.
